name: Tesamorelin

lead: Tesamorelin (Egrifta) is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone approved in the United States to reduce excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy. It is injected daily.

It is sometimes discussed in body-composition and peptide circles for visceral fat reduction. Its approval and evidence cover only that specific patient group, and it has not been shown to remove fat from the cheeks or jawline selectively.

paras: Tesamorelin stimulates the pituitary to release endogenous growth hormone in a pulsatile fashion, which raises IGF-1. Growth hormone promotes lipolysis, with a particular effect on visceral adipose tissue, which explains the reduction in trunk fat in trials.

Reported effects include joint pain, fluid retention, injection-site reactions and glucose intolerance, and raised IGF-1 prompts caution about malignancy. It is prescription-only and costly, fat returns after stopping, and benefits in people without HIV lipodystrophy are not established.

lead: Tesamorelin (brand names Egrifta, Egrifta SV and Egrifta WR) is a synthetic analogue of growth-hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) made by Theratechnologies of Canada. It was approved by the US FDA in November 2010 for reducing excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy and is given by daily subcutaneous injection [1][2][3].

It stimulates the pituitary to release endogenous growth hormone in a pulsatile pattern, raising IGF-1 and promoting lipolysis, with a particular effect on visceral fat [3][1]. The label states it is not indicated for weight loss management, as its effect on weight is neutral, and that long-term cardiovascular safety has not been established [3].

In bodybuilding and peptide forums it is discussed as a growth-hormone secretagogue, often paired with ipamorelin, for fat loss and raising IGF-1 [4][5][6]. Approval and trial evidence cover HIV-associated abdominal fat; the drug is not known to remove fat from the face or any specific site selectively, and benefits in people without HIV lipodystrophy have not been established in the cited trials.
infobox: 44 amino acids of human GHRH plus a trans-3-hexenoyl group

paras: Egrifta SV is indicated for the reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy. The label's limitations state that it is not indicated for weight loss, that no data show improved adherence to antiretroviral therapy, and that treatment should be reconsidered in patients who do not reduce visceral fat [3].

Forum users describe using tesamorelin off-label in combination with other peptides such as ipamorelin, or alongside testosterone and anabolic compounds, to raise IGF-1 and reduce fat [4][7][8]. One poster on T Nation argues that GH-related products lower fat and cites tesamorelin's approval as support [9]. These uses are outside the approved indication, and the label's evidence concerns HIV lipodystrophy.

The pivotal trial randomized 412 people with HIV, 86 percent men, who had abdominal fat accumulation, to daily tesamorelin or placebo to test whether visceral adiposity could be reduced [10]. A pooled analysis of two phase 3 trials with safety extension data and a separate randomized trial with a safety extension reported visceral fat outcomes [11][12]. A 2014 JAMA trial examined visceral and liver fat and an HIV-associated NAFLD trial reported liver fat reductions and prevention of fibrosis progression over one year [13][14][15]. A trial in people with HIV on integrase inhibitors was published in 2024 [16]. Tesamorelin has also been tested in type 2 diabetes, obese people with reduced GH, and for cognition and inflammatory markers [17][18][19][20][21]. Pharmacy-journal reviews summarize efficacy and safety in HIV lipodystrophy [2].

The most commonly reported adverse reactions include joint pain, injection-site reactions, fluid retention and peripheral edema, diarrhea and glucose intolerance [3][1]. The label warns of increased risk of neoplasms, elevated IGF-1, fluid retention, glucose intolerance or diabetes, hypersensitivity and injection-site reactions; pre-existing malignancy should be inactive before starting and IGF-1 should be monitored [3]. It is contraindicated in pregnancy, and in rats exposure during organogenesis caused hydrocephaly in offspring [3]. Wikipedia also lists contraindication in hypothalamic-pituitary axis disruption such as pituitary tumor, head irradiation or hypopituitarism [1].

Tesamorelin binds human GHRH receptors with potency similar to the endogenous hormone and stimulates synthesis and pulsatile release of growth hormone, which is anabolic and lipolytic [3]. The modified N-terminus makes it more stable and more resistant to cleavage by dipeptidyl peptidase than native GHRH [1]. The main mechanisms by which it reduces fat mass are lipolysis and lower triglycerides [1].

T Nation threads discuss tesamorelin among growth-hormone peptides, with members comparing IGF-1 results from combinations with ipamorelin or CJC-1295 and noting that these secretagogues do not stimulate hunger the way some GHRPs do [22][5][4][7]. Posters also report using it alongside oxandrolone or testosterone and note its cost [8][7]. Reviews of peptide therapy in sports medicine and aesthetics describe a gray market of unapproved peptides outside regulatory oversight [23][24].

Tesamorelin has randomized phase 3 data in HIV-associated abdominal fat [10][11][12][13], randomized data on liver fat in HIV-associated NAFLD [14][15], and smaller trials in type 2 diabetes, obesity with reduced growth hormone, cognition and inflammatory markers [17][18][19][20]. No published trial has tested tesamorelin for cosmetic fat loss in healthy people or for facial appearance.

lore.intro: Tesamorelin appears in T Nation discussions of growth-hormone peptides, usually alongside ipamorelin or CJC-1295, with attention to IGF-1 numbers and fat loss [22][5][4].

claims.claim: Tesamorelin plus ipamorelin raises IGF-1 more than other secretagogue blends.
Tesamorelin lowers fat, so GH-related products lower fat in general.
The tesamorelin/ipamorelin blend avoids growth hormone's side effects.
It does not stimulate hunger like some growth-hormone peptides.
Low-dose tesamorelin works for fat loss when stacked with anabolics.
GH-axis drugs can change facial features at normal doses.
